simple.meaning: מְרֹרָה (mᵉrôrâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, bitterness ; concretely, a bitter thing ; specifically bile ; also venom (of a serpent).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מְרֹרָה (H4846) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:32, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, Job.

simple.summary: מְרֹרָה (mᵉrôrâh) / H4846 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:32, Job 13:26, Job 20:14, Job 20:25 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, bitterness ; concretely, a bitter thing ; specifically bile ; also venom (of a serpent)
definitions.full: H4846. merorah [ מְרֹרָה ] noun feminine bitter thing, gall, poison ; construct מְרוֺרַת Job 20:14 ; suffix מְרֹרָתוֺ 20:25 ; plural מְרֹרֹת Deut 32:32 , מְרֹרוֺת Job 13:36; — 1 gall , i.e. seat of gall, gall-bladder Job 20:25 (|| גֵּוָה back ; compare מְרֵרָה Job 16:30). 2 = poison , ׳מ מְּתָנִים Job 20:14 . 3 מְרֹרוֺת bitter thing Job 13:26 (of God's edict of judgment). 4 plural abstract = bitterness ; ׳מ אַשְׁכְּלֹת Deut 32:32 clusters of bitterness (|| רוֺשׁ עִנְּבְי ).

occurrences.englishText: For their vine is of the vine of Sodom,
For you write bitter things against me,
yet his food in his bowels is turned.
He draws it out, and it comes out of his body.
